home.heroSubtitle: Wines shaped by hand, patience, and a piece of Italian hillside.
home.introTitle: A family winery, made the slow way
home.introText: For three generations, the Valletti family has tended the same hillside vineyards, working with the seasons rather than against them. Every bottle carries the mark of that patience — and of Roberto Valletti, who still walks the rows every morning.
home.philosophyTeaserText: Minimal intervention, native yeasts, and a deep respect for the land. Learn how Roberto makes wine the way his grandfather taught him — only better.

winery.title: The Winery
winery.openingLine: When family winemaking tradition, academic knowledge and innovation come together, there is an opportunity to create truly exceptional wines.
winery.philosophyQuote: Great wine is about identity. It is about unlocking the full potential of two interconnected worlds: the terroir and the cellar. Neither can compensate for the other. There are no shortcuts to excellence.
winery.vineyardText1: The journey always begins in the vineyard. Producing outstanding wine requires dedication, patience and an uncompromising commitment to creating the best possible conditions for the vines. Every decision, from soil management to canopy management and yield control, is made with one purpose in mind: ensuring that only the finest grapes become part of the final wine.
winery.vineyardText2: For the Valletti estate, understanding and continuously improving the terroir has always been a fundamental principle. Generations of family experience have been combined with academic knowledge and a willingness to embrace innovation in order to reveal the unique character of each vineyard. The objective has never been to produce wine that simply reflects a grape variety, but to capture the identity of the land itself.
winery.harvestText1: Every year, as August approaches, attention shifts from the vineyard to the cellar. Harvest is one of the most important and demanding periods of the year, where experience, timing and careful planning determine the quality of the vintage.
winery.harvestText2: There is only a small window in which each grape variety reaches its optimal ripeness. Harvesting too early can result in wines lacking complexity and balance, while harvesting too late may compromise freshness and structure. Every vineyard, and often every individual parcel, is monitored closely to ensure that each grape is picked at precisely the right moment.
winery.cellarText1: Once the grapes arrive at the cellar, the next stage of the journey begins. Each variety, and ultimately each wine, is carefully handled according to its unique characteristics and the style that the Valletti estate wishes to express. From fermentation and extraction to ageing and blending, every decision shapes the experience that will eventually be found in the bottle.
winery.cellarText2: No two vintages are ever the same. Sunshine, rainfall, temperature fluctuations and countless other natural influences ensure that every harvest presents a new set of opportunities and challenges. Rather than following a rigid formula, Roberto Valletti allows each vintage to guide his decisions. Drawing on generations of family knowledge, supported by academic expertise and a continuous drive to innovate, he adapts every stage of the winemaking process to express the very best of that particular year.
winery.closingQuote: The cellar is not a place where great wine is created. It is where the potential that has been carefully nurtured in the vineyard is preserved, refined and respectfully expressed. The role of the winemaker is not to change the character of the grapes, but to reveal it.
winery.closingText: This philosophy has guided the Valletti family for generations. Exceptional wine is never the result of chance. It is the product of tradition, scientific understanding, innovation and relentless attention to detail, from the first work in the vineyard to the moment the wine is poured into the glass. Every bottle is an expression of the Valletti family's commitment to authenticity, quality and respect for the land that makes it all possible.

about.title: About Valletti
about.intro: A story that begins with one hillside and a family that never wanted to leave it.
about.historyText: In 1958, Roberto's grandfather, Alessandro Valletti, planted the first rows of Dolcetto on a steep, stony hillside that most of his neighbours considered too difficult to farm. He was wrong about it being difficult — it just required patience. His son Marco expanded the estate in the 1980s, and today Roberto Valletti continues the work, having taken over the cellar in 2005 after studying oenology and working harvests across Italy and France.
about.todayText: Today the estate spans a small number of carefully tended hectares across two vineyard sites. We remain a family operation — Roberto in the vineyard and cellar, with his wife Elena managing the estate and welcoming visitors. We produce a limited number of wines each year, all from our own grapes, all made on site.
about.robertoText: Roberto took over winemaking from his father in 2005. He trained in Alba and spent harvests in Burgundy before returning home, convinced that the family's hillside had more to say than anyone had yet let it.

wines.title: Our Wines
wines.intro: Each wine we make reflects a specific plot, a specific grape, and a specific moment in the Valletti calendar. Select a wine to learn more.

visit.title: Visit Us
visit.intro: Roberto and Elena welcome visitors to the estate for tastings and vineyard walks by appointment. Tell us a little about what you're looking for and we'll get back to you.
visit.openingHoursText: Visits by appointment only — get in touch and we'll find a time that works. Typically Monday–Saturday, 10:00–17:00.
